podcast.title: Hip-Hop Collaboration with Timbaland That Debuted at #10 and Dropped 55 Places
podcast.body: After Audioslave broke up, Cornell teamed with hip-hop producer Timbaland for a solo album that replaced guitars and rock with beats and a pop/hip-hop approach. The album debuted at number 10 on the charts and then dropped 55 spots the following week — one of the biggest single-week falls from the top 10 in chart history. Even Trent Reznor publicly commented that Cornell had embarrassed himself. Cornell was eventually able to recover from the setback and reunite Soundgarden. "Even Trent Reznor felt he had to say something, quoted as saying that Chris had embarrassed himself."

podcast.title: Collaboration with Timberland
podcast.body: This album was recorded with hip-hop performer and producer Timberland. The collaboration was a significant departure from Cornell's grunge roots and was met with commercial disappointment. It connected Chris Cornell professionally to a wide range of R&B and hip-hop artists. "The result, which was called scream, how do we put this? Well, it was a commercial disappointment and more."

podcast.body: Chris Cornell collaborated with producer Timbaland for this album, shifting from his previous rock records to an R&B and hip-hop sound. The album was recorded in just six weeks, featuring drum machines, R&B grooves, and samples instead of heavy guitars and rock rhythms. The cover artwork depicted Cornell jumping, "apparently ready to smash a guitar." It was a "critical and commercial disaster." "It was if Chris Cornell was trying to be Justin Timberlake."
